title: A no-bid reason code outside both the canonical list and the exchange-specific range is not distinguished from a real one
specNotes: This mutation is paired with mut-input-shape-nbr-exchange-specific, which uses nbr=700 (a valid exchange-specific code) to show the tool treats both identically today — the missing check is the ability to tell them apart, not a rejection of code 42 outright (an unassigned code is not itself an error, only unremarkable-worthy).

`expected.response.nbr_code_unassigned` is a descriptive placeholder id, not a real Core finding id: this records a missing capability, modeled directly on the existing `imp.video.protocols_unknown` pattern (out-of-range enum values outside the reserved exchange band get a WARNING) for the same shape of enumeration on the response side.
response.no_bid still fires correctly (nbr is a number, seatbid absent) — the gap is the absence of a second, code-quality finding alongside it, not a false claim about the no-bid shape itself.
Browser measured on 2026-09-08 in run ortbtools-audit-9fSncA; only the exact observed product deviations are admitted. Normative finding and successful-analysis assertions are retained.
